Que un compilador tuviera que optimizar: That a compiler should have to optimise was not a later improvement: it was the condition for its being accepted. When John Backus's team started FORTRAN in 1954, the argument against was unanimous: an automatically translated program would be slower than a hand-written one, and machine time cost a fortune. So they set themselves the goal that the generated code should be comparable to that of a good assembly programmer, and a good part of the project's two and a half years went into the optimiser. They managed it, and that is the reason hardly anybody writes assembly by hand today: not because it cannot be done, but because the compiler usually does it better.
